metadata.title: The gender system: A cross-national perspective

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 microdata covering 15-year-old students across 80 countries/economies, but it excludes Lebanon and North Macedonia (substantial missingness) and Kosovo (missing country-level data), and removes subnational regions with separate representative samples (e.g., Moscow, Tatarstan). The paper does not report the specific PISA student weight variable name or whether complex survey weights were applied in the structure-learning and predictive modeling steps. Because the analysis relies on a structure-learning algorithm (Hill-Climbing in bnlearn) and Lasso logistic regression, the manuscript does not document a weighting strategy; therefore, weight usage cannot be confirmed from the provided text. Missingness is handled via stochastic regression multiple imputation (chained equations) with country fixed effects, and country-level predictors are imputed similarly.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: plausible_values_handling is 'not_applicable' — the study likely does not analyze cognitive achievement PVs (e.g., it may focus on affective/attitudinal outcomes, curriculum data, or non-ILSA micro-data).

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2018 main student questionnaire data for 15-year-olds across 80 countries/economies, excluding Lebanon and North Macedonia due to substantial missingness (omitted half the items), excluding Kosovo due to missing country-level data, and removing subnational regions with separate representative samples (e.g., Moscow and Tatarstan) to avoid double-counting. Additional country-specific questionnaire modules were excluded when administered by fewer than half of participating countries/economies. For the structure-learning search, only items included by each country were used (if a country did not include a specific item, that item was omitted from that country-specific search).

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 (15-year-olds) — competitiveness as constitutive element of gender (cross-national, country-specific graphical models)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Lasso logistic regression (competitiveness): test-data cross-validation accuracy = 0.79. Linear probability model: 1 SD increase in women education and training associated with +22.4 percentage points in competitiveness (SE = 0.040); controlling for development index: β = 0.249, SE = 0.040. Correlation between country sex differences in competitiveness and women education/training: r = -0.7.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 the study leveraged women education and training (plus other country-level gender-inequality indices and region) to predict whether competitiveness is identified as a constitutive element of gender, finding that women’s education and training is the strongest predictor and is associated with a large increase in the probability that competitiveness differentiates boys and girls. This indicates that expanding women’s educational and economic opportunities may shift which traits become gender-differentiating in schooling contexts, though the analysis is explicitly predictive and observational (no causal identification).

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 (15-year-olds) — empathy as constitutive element of gender (cross-national, country-specific graphical models)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Lasso logistic regression (empathy): test-data cross-validation accuracy = 0.76. Empathy inclusion rates: 60% of Asian countries vs 13% of European countries vs none in the Americas.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 the study leveraged region (especially whether a country is in Asia) and other country-level gender-related indicators to predict whether empathy is identified as a constitutive element of gender, finding that Asia is the strongest predictor and that empathy is far more likely to function as a gender-differentiating attribute in Asian countries than in Europe or the Americas. This indicates that gendered trait construction in education may be strongly context- and region-dependent, suggesting that interventions or gender-typicality assumptions should be localized rather than treated as universal.

data.outcome_summary: This paper uses PISA 2018 microdata for 15-year-old students across 72 countries/regions (after excluding Lebanon and North Macedonia for missingness and Kosovo for missing country-level data, and removing subnational regions with separate samples). It first applies a structure-learning algorithm (Hill-Climbing in bnlearn) within each country to identify the “neighbors” of sex in a probabilistic graphical model, interpreted as the constitutive elements of gender. It then fits Lasso logistic regression models to predict whether two traits—competitiveness and cognitive empathy (perspective-taking)—are present as constitutive elements, using 19 country-level predictors from major gender equality indices plus WVS subjective measures, human development, collectivism, and region. Cross-validation accuracy is 0.79 for competitiveness and 0.76 for empathy. Missing individual and country-level data are imputed via stochastic regression in chained equations, but the manuscript does not document PISA sampling-weight usage, and the approach is explicitly predictive rather than causal.
